https://english.wafa.ps/Pages/Details/17.text: Français العربية Info Images Thursday , 03 September , 2026 Weather + 29 ° C + 29° + 20° Ramallah Wednesday, 08 Thursday + 27° + 16° Friday + 28° + 15° Saturday + 29° + 15° Sunday + 30° + 17° Monday + 30° + 18° Tuesday + 30° + 16° See 7-Day Forecast Menu Tulkarm: Israeli forces raid Iktaba suburb, raid and search homes Occupation forces raid home, threaten resident with expulsion in Tubas plain PM Mustafa discusses joint efforts with Japan’s assistant Foreign Minister for Gaza Reconstruction and Humanitarian Recovery Civil Affairs Authority receives slain youth's body killed by Israel after it'd been held since November Poland condemns Israel's closure of investigation into World Central Kitchen convoy attack WARSAW, August 20, 2026 (WAFA) — Poland's Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Thursday expressed disappointment over Israel's decision to close its investigation into the targeting of a World Central Kitchen (WCK) volunteer convoy in the Gaza Strip on April 1, 2024, which killed seven foreign aid workers, including Polish national Damian Soból, as well as Palestinian workers affiliated with the organization. In a statement, the ministry said it had summoned the Israeli ambassador to Warsaw and conveyed its condemnation and rejection of the measures taken so far, while demanding clarification of the causes and circumstances surrounding the tragedy. The ministry noted that the case is also being investigated by the Regional Prosecutor’s Office in the Polish city of Przemyśl, Soból’s hometown. It said Poland expects Israel to provide the relevant Polish authorities with all explanations and materials requested by Polish investigators. Poland's Foreign Ministry stressed that the circumstances surrounding the 2024 tragedy must be fully clarified and said it would not accept attempts by those responsible to evade their legal and moral accountability. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm98.text: Image source, Getty Image caption, Australia will cut immigration by cracking down on international students and backpackers, Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke says By Lana Lam Sydney Published 17 September 2026, 06:05 BST International students, so-called "visa hoppers" and backpackers will be targeted under stricter rules announced by Australia on Thursday in a bid to curb immigration. Foreign students will no longer be able to bring their families with them and those who want to extend their stay must choose a higher qualification. Rules will also be stricter for working holiday visas - commonly used by backpackers and a crucial labour source for the agricultural sector - with a ballot system although these changes will not affect the UK. The new rules were revealed by Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke who said that while immigration was a "strength" of Australia, there needed to be a "high level of control". For international student and graduate visas, Burke said: "We will no longer be adding to the stock of students automatically being able to bring family members over." There would be exemptions for foreign students already in Australia as well as applicants from the Pacific and South East Asian countries, he said. PhD students would also be able to bring their families as they were in different life circumstances to undergraduates, Burke said. In a speech titled "The work of managing the migration program: who arrives, who stays, who leaves", Burke revealed a raft of changes as the government aims to bring net overseas migration to 225,000 people by 2028. On student visas, he said the government would clamp down on "visa hopping" - where a student finishes a course, then applies to do another course which is often a lower qualification and sometimes with a "not so legitimate provider". Students who want to go "up the scale" will be allowed, Burke said, for example, if a student finishes a bachelor's degree and then wants to complete a masters. He also announced major changes to working holiday visas for those aged 18 to 30 years old who can work in Australia for 12 months, but can extend for a second and third year. Currently, these visa holders must work for three months in regional Australia during their first year to qualify for a second year, and then six months to qualify for a third year. Under the new changes, those who qualify for a second year will have to go into a ballot with a cap of 45,000, down from the 57,000 who qualified last year. For the third year, the ballot will be limited to 5,000, down from 31,000 who qualified last year. British working holidaymakers will not be affected by these changes due to the UK's free trade agreement with Australia. New figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics on Thursday showed Australia's population grew 1.4% in the 12 months to March 2026 to 27.9m. That total figure included births and deaths as well as a net overseas migration of 292,100. Migration remains a major political issue as debate around Australia's population grows amid rising living costs, housing affordability and increased strain on public services. One Nation, a populist right-wing party known for its anti-immigration stance and which has seen a surge in support in recent months, detailed its migration policy earlier this week, proposing to cut temporary migrant visas by 750,000 over three years. The party, which won its first lower house seat in May , also wants to cap net overseas immigration to 130,000, drawing a rebuke from Burke who said such a proposal would risk "smashing parts of the Australian economy". In July, the government introduced a policy to prioritise applications for family visas lodged onshore - where the applicant is in the country already - over those submitted overseas. Skilled migrants already in Australia who applied for permanent visas were also prioritised over those applying from overseas. It also paused applications for working holiday visas from 24 countries, not including the UK. Violet Roumeliotis, from Settlement Services International which helps new arrivals to Australia, says the migration debate was increasingly driven by "short-term politics rather than what is best for the country". "The proposed changes to family visas for international students is a good example of this," she said, adding that it would make it harder for Australia to compete for "future talent". https://telex.hu/english/2026/11/23/magy.text: Hungarian lawmakers started an unusually long sitting of parliament on Monday, which is set to run from Monday through Friday, as well as on Monday the following week. During this time, they will debate a total of twenty-seven bills. Prime Minister Péter Magyar addressed Parliament before the start of daily business. He began his speech by commenting on the drone attack against Transcarpathia (home to the Hungarian ethnic minority in Ukraine) last week, during which one of the drones crashed near the Mukachevo train station. “Just imagine what that morning must have been like in Mukachevo, with people calling their mothers just to confirm that they were safe,” said the Prime Minister. Magyar recalled the story of his grandfather, who also had to flee from bombs. “When my grandfather was 10 years old, he crossed the frozen Tisza River to get to Mukachevo so he could retrieve the family heirlooms left behind, and then set off again toward Debrecen as bombs continued to fall all around him.” According to the Prime Minister, this is precisely why the matter of Hungarians living in neighbouring countries will never be a simple question of foreign policy. “Ukraine and our fellow Hungarians living in the country have been enduring unimaginable suffering for nearly five years,” Péter Magyar said, adding that he believes that the war’s most brutal winter may be just around the corner. The Prime Minister said that when Transcarpathia was hit last week, he was reminded of his 2024 visit to Kyiv and Transcarpathia to deliver donations. During the visit, he and members of the Tisza Party delivered donations to a children’s hospital that had been hit by a Russian missile shortly before. He recalled what it was like to arrive in the barricaded, blacked-out city of Kyiv and that upon arriving at their hotel, they were first shown the bomb shelter, and how to use the emergency alert app. Addressing the Fidesz and KDNP representatives directly, he noted that Viktor Orbán had not been to Transcarpatchia since the outbreak of the war. “From here in the Hungarian Parliament, I would like to express my solidarity with the people of Transcarpathia and with the whole Ukrainian nation, who have been waging an unprecedented struggle for survival for the past five years,” he said, adding that he wanted to make it clear that in this war, Russia is the aggressor and Ukraine is the victim. Magyar’s statement was met with applause from the representatives of Tisza, but the representatives of Fidesz, KDNP, and Mi Hazánk did not applaud. To this, Magyar commented that they should be ashamed of themselves. The leader of the Tisza Party then recalled that after the attack on Transcarpathia, Fidesz issued a statement suggesting that it was his fault that the Russians had bombed Transcarpathia. He opined that it was time to make it clear that not he, but the Russians alone were responsible for the attack. He also said that he considers it a crime that Fidesz responded to the outbreak of the Russian-Ukrainian war with a hate campaign against Ukrainians; and added that it was not true that the Russians did not attack Transcarpathia during the previous government’s term. The last time a Hungarian prime minister visited Transcarpathia was in 2015, Péter Magyar noted, before announcing that he would soon be going there, with the intention to personally deliver a message from the motherland to the Hungarian minority living in the country. The PM did not specify exactly when he would travel to Ukraine, nor did he mention whether he would meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky during his visit. The last time Péter Magyar briefly met with Volodymyr Zelensky was during the European Political Community summit on November 12, when the possibility of a future official meeting was discussed. At that time, Magyar said that the meeting would not take place in Budapest or Kyiv, but most likely in Transcarpathia, and that the two countries' foreign ministers would be working out the details. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha announced on November 18 that Péter Magyar and Volodymyr Zelensky would meet before November was over. Last week, at the EU Foreign Affairs Council meeting in Brussels, Sybiha and Anita Orbán agreed to capitalize on the positive developments in bilateral relations and finalize arrangements for the high-level meeting before November’s end. During Monday’s speech, the Prime Minister also touched on his upcoming trip to the EC Summit later this week and noted that there are political forces that would like to shift the focus of the negotiations on the next EU budget to how Ukraine will be financed in the future. According to Magyar, this issue must be addressed separately. “Hungary will continue to provide Ukraine with whatever assistance it can from a humanitarian perspective,” he said. Péter Magyar said that in the second half of this week, when he sits down at the negotiating table in the EU, he will carry with him the stories of the farmer struggling with drought and the entrepreneur seeking fair competition. According to the Hungarian Prime Minister, the 10 billion euros that have just been brought home were a debt of the past, while the next seven-year budget belongs to the future. He said that the budget cuts proposed by António Costa, the President of the European Council over the weekend are unacceptable for Hungary. “We, Hungarians, are full members of this community; we have the right to have a say in what kind of future we are building,” he said. https://hvg.hu/eurologus/20261126_robert.text: Az Európai Parlament kész konstruktívan részt venni a következő, 2028 és 2034 közötti uniós költségvetésről szóló tárgyalásokban, de nem fog automatikusan rábólintani a tagállami vezetők megállapodására – jelentette ki Roberta Metsola, az Európai Parlament elnöke a brüsszeli EU-csúcs alkalmával tartott sajtótájékoztatóján. Ahogy mindig, Metsola most is részt vett a tagállami vezetők tárgyalásának elején, ismertette az EP álláspontját a következő hétéves költségvetés, illetve Ukrajna további támogatása kapcsán. Ezt követően az újságírók előtt hangsúlyozta: a költségvetés elfogadásához legalább 361 európai parlamenti képviselő támogatására lesz szükség, ezért a tagállamoknak már a tárgyalások során figyelembe kell venniük az EP álláspontját. A Parlament nem egy gumibélyegző. Soha nem volt az, és soha nem is lesz – fogalmazott Metsola, arra a kérdésre válaszolva, hogy az EP megvétózhatja-e a tagállamok között születő kompromisszumot. Hozzátette: nem akarja előre megjósolni a szavazás eredményét, de ha a Tanács figyelembe veszi a Parlament már áprilisban elfogadott előzetes álláspontját, az megkönnyítheti a tárgyalásokat. Metsola négy fő prioritást nevezett meg. Az első a gazdasági növekedés ösztönzése. Az uniós költségvetést nem egyszerű kiadási keretként, hanem befektetési tervként kell kezelni, amelynek a gazdaságot, a munkahelyteremtést, a biztonságot és az energiát kell szolgálnia. Érvelése szerint minden befektetett euró hozzávetőleg háromeurónyi gazdasági hasznot termel az európai polgárok és vállalkozások számára. Második prioritásként azt emelte ki, hogy az uniós költségvetés eredményeinek a mindennapi életben is érzékelhetőnek kell lenniük. Az európai ambícióknak kézzelfogható fejlesztésekben kell megjelenniük, például felújított iskolákban, korszerűsített kórházakban és jobb közlekedési infrastruktúrában. Ezzel összefüggésben komoly problémának nevezte, hogy a tervek alapján több mint 46 milliárd euróval csökkenne a kohéziós támogatások összege a jelenlegi költségvetési időszakhoz képest, azonos árakon számolva. A harmadik kérdés az új uniós saját források megteremtése, ezen belül a digitális szolgáltatásokra kivetendő adó. Az Európai Parlament támogatja az új bevételi forrásokat, mert ezek segíthetnének a korábbi közös adósság visszafizetésében, miközben csökkentenék a tagállami költségvetésekre nehezedő nyomást. A digitális adó azonban vitatott elképzelés: Micheál Martin ír miniszterelnök a csúcsra érkezve határozottan ellenezte, arra hivatkozva, hogy szerinte ellentétes az európai versenyképesség érdekeivel. Metsola szerint a saját források kérdése kulcsfontosságú a költségvetési kompromisszumhoz. A múlt kifizetése nem történhet a jövőbe történő beruházások rovására – hangsúlyozta. Úgy vélte, az új bevételek teremthetik meg a hidat a tagállamok eltérő álláspontjai között, és lehetővé tehetik, hogy az EU valóban megfeleljen a megváltozott gazdasági és biztonsági környezet kihívásainak. Negyedik prioritásként Ukrajna támogatását nevezte meg. Kijevnek kiszámítható, fenntartható és hiteles finanszírozásra van szüksége, miközben Európának továbbra is támogatnia kell az országot az igazságos és tartós béke eléréséig. Metsola hangsúlyozta, hogy ez nem csupán szolidaritási kérdés, hanem Európa saját biztonságába történő befektetés is. A tárgyalások menetrendjéről szólva elmondta: a Parlament a húsz szakpolitikai területből tizenhat esetében már kialakította tárgyalási mandátumát, négy azonban még hátravan. Ezek a legnehezebb dossziék közé tartoznak, mivel a mezőgazdaságot és a nemzeti terveket érintik, és három parlamenti szakbizottság dolgozik rajtuk. Metsola szerint ugyanakkor reális, hogy a Tanács megállapodását követően még a jövőre esedékes tagállami választások előtt megszülessen az EP jóváhagyása is. Az EP elnöke végül arra szólított fel, hogy a politikai csoportok a kompromisszumot elsősorban a parlamenti centrum körül építsék fel. Szerinte az Európai Parlament akkor van a legerősebb tárgyalási pozícióban, ha széles, középről kiinduló többség támogatja az álláspontját. Nem sok jót ígérő vizsgálatok várnak a Fidesz propagandagyáraira, Mészáros Lőrinc kiszállóban.
